Act as the implementation sub-agent for this task.

Repo: inkling (Electron + React + TS, Bun, Windows app). Read AGENTS.md at the repo root and follow it (verifying rules, docs rules, PR rules, the "three ways to hurt yourself"). Do the work yourself; no subagents. This machine is Windows; use Bun APIs with argument arrays, no shell string commands, and no bash-only syntax in the script.

## Goal
Add `bun run check:changed`: one command an agent or dev runs while iterating and before pushing. It runs the fast subset of CI's checks for only what the branch changed. `bun run check` (the full CI mirror) stays as is. Inspiration is t3code's `scripts/check-changed.ts` (https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/blob/main/scripts/check-changed.ts), but ours must be much smaller: yagni, aim for roughly 100 lines. Do NOT copy its run-result cache, workspace/affected-package mapping, patch check, or GraphQL parts.

## Behavior
- `bun run check:changed` compares against `git merge-base HEAD origin/main`; optional first argument is another ref. If there is no merge base, print a one-line hint to `git fetch origin` and exit 1.
- Changed files = `git diff --name-only --no-renames <base>` plus untracked files (`git ls-files --others --exclude-standard`). Only files that still exist are passed to tools. No changes -> print so and exit 0.
- Steps (run concurrently, print each step's output when it finishes, then a pass/fail summary, exit non-zero if any failed):
  1. `oxlint` on changed JS/TS files (`bunx oxlint <files>` or the local binary; match how package.json's `lint` script invokes it).
  2. `oxfmt --check` on changed files oxfmt handles. Make sure files in `.oxfmtrc.json` ignorePatterns (md, yml, bun.lock, etc.) are not passed in a way that makes oxfmt error with "no target files"; test this with a docs-only change and with an ignored file.
  3. `bun test` on changed test files plus sibling tests of changed source files (`foo.ts` -> `foo.test.ts` in the same directory; also `.test.tsx`). Skip the step when none.
  4. `bun run knip` when any code file or package.json/knip.json changed.
  5. `bun run typecheck` when any code or tsconfig/package.json changed (it is fast enough to run whole).
- Must work on Windows (backslash paths from git are forward-slash; normalize anyway) and in a git worktree.

## Also update (same change)
- `package.json`: add the `check:changed` script.
- `t3.json`: add a matching run script entry (AGENTS.md requires t3.json to stay in sync with package.json scripts).
- `AGENTS.md` "Verifying": the first bullet currently hand-composes `bun test <files>`, `bunx oxlint <files>`, `bunx oxfmt --check <files>`, `bun run typecheck`. Replace that with `bun run check:changed` as the pre-push command (keep `bun test <files>` for fast iteration and keep the "do not run repo-wide checks" rule and the note that `bun run check` mirrors CI). Edit only that bullet; do not touch "Where code lives" or "How it works" (other open PRs edit those).
- `docs/operations/development.md`: add it where the commands/checks are listed. Keep it to a line or two.
- `bun run check:refs` must pass (it validates command references in docs).
- Skip the changelog (internal dev tooling, trivial per docs rules) unless docs/changelog.md's header says otherwise.
- A test only if the file-to-test mapping has non-obvious logic; do not add trivial tests. Prove it works by running `bun run check:changed` on your own branch's changes, on a docs-only change, on an empty diff, and once with a deliberately broken lint/test change (revert it afterwards). Report the observed results.

## Delivery (full-stop: PR ready for the user, never merged by you)
- Branch from latest origin/main (`git fetch origin; git switch -c chore/check-changed origin/main`). Other PRs are open, so keep the diff to the files above.
- Conventional commit, e.g. `chore(scripts): add check:changed for fast pre-push checks`. End the commit message with your own `Co-Authored-By: <your model name> <noreply@anthropic.com>` line.
- Push and open a PR with `gh` (use the `file-pr` skill if you have it). Body: the problem in a sentence or two (agents hand-assemble checks), how you fixed it, one line on how you verified, and end with your model name and harness `(T3 Code)`, then `🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)`.
- Never merge, enable auto-merge, or push to main. Do not call watch_pull_request; do not poll or sleep. Look at check state once.
- Last line of your final message exactly: `PR <full URL>, head <SHA>, checks and reviews <state>`. Above it, 3-6 lines on what you did and any doubts.

## Checks

| Goal | Command | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Everything | `bun run check` | Bun pin, frozen install (`--ignore-scripts`), typecheck of every workspace, tests, Knip, lint, both builds, ingestion smoke, extension build. CI runs the same steps as separate jobs |
| Typecheck | `bun run typecheck` | App, benchmark harness, and `electron/` |
| Tests | `bun test` | |
| Unused code | `bun run knip` | Hard gate in CI; `knip.json` owns entry/project patterns. To clean up locally, run `bunx knip --fix` then `bun install` (re-syncs the lockfile if deps were pruned), fix any `noUnusedLocals` fallout, and re-run `bun run check` |
| Lint and format | `bun run lint` (`bun run lint:fix` to apply) | oxlint, with inkling rules in `oxlint-plugin-inkling/`, then oxfmt |
| Bun pin | `bun run check:bun-version` | running Bun must match `.bun-version` |
| Extension build | `bun run --cwd extension build` | Builds the Chrome MV3 extension and its service worker |

For early signal, run `bun run check`. `noUnusedLocals` / `noUnusedParameters` are on — the compiler catches dead locals; Knip catches dead exports and dependencies.
